solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Devoted woman with more frumpy clothing I left a long way away

indicators.note: to clothe something is to wrap round it, so the trimmed frumpy word goes around the devoted woman
left in the sense of departed: the letter I goes out of the frumpy word

parts.note: frumpy means dowdy, so more frumpy is dowdier
a nun is a woman devoted to religious life

explanation.surface: A pious woman in drab clothes has walked off and gone a long way from home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' gives DOWDER, which 'clothing' wraps round the devoted woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal name for Australia and New Zealand, the far side of the globe as seen from Britain.

clue.text: Maiden forced to eat up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the letters are read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: someone force-fed through a tube, like a hunger striker, has been tubed

explanation.surface: A young woman being made to finish her plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses TUBED in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Maiden as an adjective means first, as in a maiden speech, which is a first appearance.

clue.text: Ring found in small sort of cushion

indicators.note: the ring is found inside the word for small

parts.note: wee is Scottish and informal for small
a hoop is a ring

explanation.surface: A ring discovered inside a little cushion.
explanation.definitionFit: A whoopee cushion is a joke rubber cushion that makes a rude noise when sat on.

clue.text: Not protected, but treated civilly, perhaps, about answer

indicators.note: about means around, so the civil treatment goes round the answer's letter

parts.note: someone treated civilly has not been insulted

explanation.surface: A cagey reply: left exposed, yet handled politely.
explanation.definitionFit: Wiring without insulation lacks its protective covering.

clue.text: Miner clear about nit needing a going over

indicators.note: a going over turns the whole assembled construction head over heels, so it is read backwards
the word for clear sits around the nit

parts.note: to clear is to rid
a nit is the egg of a louse

explanation.surface: A miner wants to get rid of head lice and needs a thorough check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' gives RIDEGG, which 'needing a going over' turns backwards. A nit is a louse egg.
explanation.definitionFit: Digger is a name for a miner, especially an Australian gold miner.

clue.text: Be supinely accepting consequence of no lottery win?

definitions.meaning: to submit meekly, like a dog lying on its back
when nobody wins the jackpot, it is carried over to the next draw

explanation.surface: Meekly accepting what happens when nobody wins the lottery.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to submit passively, and also names a jackpot carried forward to the next draw.

clue.text: Emotionally affected, having had an operation?

definitions.meaning: a surgical patient has literally been sliced open

explanation.surface: Someone upset after surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is informal for distressed, and literally describes a body that has been opened by a surgeon.

clue.text: Creature climbing across the leads?

indicators.note: the leading letters of the three words are taken, as they lead their words

explanation.surface: An animal scrambling over the lead sheeting of a roof.
explanation.walkthrough: Roof leads are sheets of lead on a roof; 'leads' also signals the opening letters. 'climbing' only paints the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet that roams over rooftops is a classic feline image.

clue.text: For the Devil, time less busy in absence of yours truly

indicators.note: the speaker's self is missing from the less-busy word

parts.note: a place less busy is emptier
yours truly is the setter, I

explanation.surface: The Devil finds work for idle hands when the speaker is away.
explanation.definitionFit: Satan is the one who lures people into sin, the great seducer.

clue.text: Game is good during separate journey

parts.note: to part is to separate

indicators.note: good falls during, so inside, the journey

parts.note: a ride is a journey

explanation.surface: A game said to be good while on a separate trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Game here means wild birds shot for sport, and this one is a classic game bird.

clue.text: Demonstrate against head of state? Caution!

parts.note: to boo is to jeer in protest
a king heads a monarchy

explanation.surface: Warning about protesting against a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: In football a caution from the referee, shown with a yellow card, is a booking.

clue.text: Bishop burned with ire, fuddled with malt

indicators.note: fuddled means confused or drunk, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A cleric burnt at the stake, angry and drunk on malt whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: Hugh Latimer, Bishop of Worcester, was burned at Oxford in 1555 as a Protestant martyr.

clue.text: Take advantage of reversing area in part

indicators.note: reversing says the whole built piece is read backwards
the area letter goes in the abbreviation for part

explanation.surface: Exploit a reversing zone in part of a car park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts A in PT, giving PAT; 'reversing' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To tap a resource is to draw on or exploit it.

clue.text: Cheers, putting out resolute "Aye"

indicators.note: putting out as in dislocating or disturbing, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Saying goodbye by voicing a firm yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheers is British informal for goodbye, and so is this farewell phrase.

clue.text: Become angry, so be unable to blow nose?

definitions.meaning: humorously, mislaying the hanky one blows into

explanation.surface: Getting cross, and so unable to clear one's nose.
explanation.definitionFit: British idiom for losing one's temper, read literally as mislaying a handkerchief.

clue.text: Touchy companion maintains resistance without limit

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold, so the companion word holds the letter

parts.note: feely partners touchy in the phrase touchy-feely
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A sensitive friend keeps up resistance with no end.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something without restriction is doing it liberally, without limit.

clue.text: In tree top see, at last, bird

indicators.note: the final letter of see goes in between the tree and the top

parts.note: a fir is a tree
a crest is a top, as of a hill

indicators.note: the final letter of the word see is taken

explanation.surface: A bird spotted finally at the top of a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' gives E, which 'In' places between tree and top.
explanation.definitionFit: The firecrest is a tiny European songbird related to the goldcrest.

clue.text: Alcoholic drink by all means to be ingested, not extreme

indicators.note: the assurance is swallowed by the drink, so goes inside it

parts.note: mead is a drink fermented from honey
sure is a reply meaning by all means

explanation.surface: Drink alcohol by all means, but not to excess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not extreme' looks like an instruction to trim letters; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A measured response is moderate and restrained.

clue.text: Two seconds before, British crowd suddenly assembled

parts.note: a flash and a mo are both very short moments

explanation.surface: A British crowd gathers in mere seconds.
explanation.definitionFit: A group arranged online to gather at once in a public place for a stunt.

clue.text: Doorstop placed back in bank from some way away

indicators.note: the reversed book goes inside the word for bank

parts.note: to bank on is to rely

indicators.note: placed back means the book's letters are read backwards

parts.note: a doorstop is jokingly a huge heavy book, a tome

explanation.surface: A doorstop pushed back into a riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: Done from a distance, as with a remote control.

clue.text: For ancient tribesman, result of attack by bird now extinct?

parts.note: the moa was a giant flightless New Zealand bird, now extinct
a bite is the mark an attack can leave

explanation.surface: An ancient man wounded by a long-gone giant bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moabites were an ancient people living east of the Dead Sea, as told in the Bible.

clue.text: Enemy besieging castle, missing every other platform

indicators.note: an army besieging surrounds, so the enemy goes round the letters

parts.note: a foe is an enemy

indicators.note: every second letter of castle is dropped

explanation.surface: A foe surrounding a castle that is falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing every other' keeps C, S, L from castle; 'besieging' puts FOE round them.
explanation.definitionFit: The forecastle is the raised deck at a ship's bow, a platform.

clue.text: Space between cells wrong, programs declared

indicators.note: declared means spoken, so it is the sound that counts

parts.note: a sin is a wrong and apps are programs

explanation.surface: Faulty software announced on a cell phone.
explanation.definitionFit: The junction gap between two nerve cells across which signals pass.

clue.text: Ultimately girl is a bit short but nimble

indicators.note: ultimately points at the last letter of girl
short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: some means a bit, as in some bread

explanation.surface: A girl who is a bit short but agile.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithe and supple, moving gracefully.

clue.text: Family all but condemned in secret

parts.note: a clan is a family

indicators.note: all but means the final letter is lost

parts.note: destined means doomed or condemned

explanation.surface: A family nearly all sentenced in secret.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something covert, kept hidden from view, is secret.

clue.text: Be reliably informed head's to be sacked immediately

indicators.note: the first letter is dismissed from the word

parts.note: to know is to be sure of something

explanation.surface: An insider learns the boss will be fired at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Right this minute, at once.

clue.text: Pull away with the others

parts.note: the rest are the others

explanation.surface: Breaking away along with the rest of the group.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrench something away by force.

clue.text: Clever remark spread around about something irrational

indicators.note: about means surrounding the irrational thing
around means turned round, so the spread is read backwards

parts.note: marge is short for margarine, a spread
pi is an irrational number

explanation.surface: A witty remark spreading round, about something absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' gives EGRAM, which 'about' wraps round the irrational number.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a short witty saying, like Wilde's quips, is a clever remark.

clue.text: Despicable man cuts judge short

indicators.note: short means the word is cut off before its end

parts.note: to rate is to judge

explanation.surface: A villain cuts a judge off mid-sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotter, someone treacherous.

clue.text: Burst of anger at explosive piece of verse

parts.note: a strop is a British informal word for a sulky temper
HE is short for high explosive

explanation.surface: A tantrum at an exploding poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanza or section of a poem, from Greek choral odes.

clue.text: Handle danger as horse bolts

indicators.note: a horse that bolts runs off, so the letter leaves

parts.note: a threat is a danger
horse is slang for heroin, whose abbreviation is H

explanation.surface: Coping with peril when a horse runs away.
explanation.walkthrough: Horse is slang for heroin, so it gives H.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat something is to deal with or handle it.

clue.text: Ray, I assumed, picked up a generous invitation

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the sound is what counts

parts.note: a beam is a ray and guessed is assumed

explanation.surface: Someone collects a person named Ray on a hunch.
explanation.definitionFit: A gracious phrase inviting someone to go ahead or help themselves.
